subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
passage: I'm Rashmi, and I live in the flat next door, so our balconies almost touch. Baljeet came into that house as a bride three weeks ago. I keep seeing the same picture: Baljeet washing steel glasses that are already clean, then asking the mother-in-law, “Is this how you like it?” The father-in-law reads his paper and says nothing. The mother-in-law answers, “Fine, fine,” without looking up, which leaves Baljeet asking again. Yesterday the husband, Sanjay, took the glasses gently. “I'll dry tonight, Ma,” he said, and stood beside Baljeet at the sink. I can't say what Baljeet feels. But the shoulders came down a little.

qa.q: What was Baljeet washing when Rashmi kept seeing the same picture?
qa.a: Baljeet was washing steel glasses that were already clean.

qa.q: What might Baljeet be feeling when asking, “Is this how you like it?” again and again?
qa.a: Baljeet seems anxious about being judged in the new house and is asking for approval, though Rashmi says the inner feeling can't be known for sure.

qa.q: What did Sanjay do that helped, and why might it matter?
qa.a: Sanjay took the glasses, offered to dry and stood beside Baljeet at the sink. A spouse who stands beside a newcomer shows the house that the two are together.

qa.q: How might the mother-in-law see Baljeet's repeated “Is this how you like it?”
qa.a: The mother-in-law may think the question needs no more than “Fine, fine,” and may not notice how unsure Baljeet feels, which is why the asking goes on.

grounding: An observer describes a newly married person joining a household with unspoken habits, feeling watched, and helped when the spouse stands beside them.

passage:
Day 2. In his wife's family home, Pranav was told which chair was his and that he must wait for the elders to eat first. He nodded and stayed silent. Her aunts asked about his salary, his mother's cooking and his plans for children. Pema kept passing him water.
Day 9. Her uncle corrected how he folded the newspaper. Pranav smiled tightly and refolded it. That evening Pema said to her father, “Papa, he's a guest and a family member both. Let him choose his chair.” Her father grunted, then laughed.
Day 30. Pranav's chair was the one by the window, and he had started asking the aunts for recipes.

qa.q: Which chair did Pranav's hosts tell him was his on Day 2?
qa.a: On Day 2 he was told which chair was his and that he must wait for the elders to eat first.

qa.q: Why did Pranav smile tightly and refold the newspaper on Day 9?
qa.a: Pranav seems to feel uncomfortable and judged in the new house, so he goes along quietly instead of objecting.

qa.q: What did Pema do that helped Pranav settle in?
qa.a: Pema kept passing him water, then spoke up to her father so that Pranav could choose his chair, standing beside him.

qa.q: How might Pema's father have seen the change by Day 30?
qa.a: Her father may have come to see Pranav as part of the family, since he laughed after the chair remark and by Day 30 Pranav sat by the window and asked the aunts for recipes.

grounding: A newly married man joins his wife's household, feels watched and evaluated on Days 2 and 9, and settles in by Day 30 with his wife beside him.
